diff --git a/README.md b/README.md --- a/README.md +++ b/README.md @@ -1,7 +1,165 @@ # fieldwise -Schema-driven document extraction with a review UI and per-field evals: define a schema, drop in -PDFs or scans, get structured data, review it next to the page, and measure accuracy across prompt -versions. +**Schema-driven document extraction with a review UI and per-field evals.** Define a schema, drop +in PDFs or receipt photos, get structured data from a vision model, review it next to the page, and +measure per-field accuracy across prompt versions — on a public dataset, with reproducible numbers. -Work in progress — assembled in small pull requests; the README grows with the measured results. +[![CI](https://github.com/ilia-muravev-dev/fieldwise/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ilia-muravev-dev/fieldwise/actions/workflows/ci.yml) +[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](./LICENSE) + +![Review page: the extracted total highlighted on the receipt it was read from](docs/images/review.png) + +## Why this exists + +I ran a document pipeline in production — scans and PDFs in, OCR, an LLM extracting structured +fields, a review UI for the humans, about 40k documents a month. The number that mattered was +field accuracy on a fixed golden set, and it only moved when it was measured the same way after +every change: 81% → 93% over four iterations of prompts and schemas. This repository is that +loop, rebuilt in the open on receipts instead of invoices: + +- **Evals first.** Every prompt version is a pull request with its measured delta. The grader is + checked by construction (an oracle scores 100%, a null baseline 0% value accuracy) and CI re-scores + recorded model responses on every push — for free. +- **Structured outputs, not regexes.** The authored JSON Schema becomes the model's output schema, + the grader's field list and the UI's tree, from one file. +- **Reviewers close the loop.** A correction saved in the UI becomes the document's golden label and + a few-shot example for similar documents. + +## Results so far + +Measured on the [CORD v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/naver-clova-ix/cord-v2) test split +(Indonesian receipts, CC BY 4.0), 20 documents, OpenRouter's free `nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro`, effort low. +Every number below is copied from a report in [`docs/evals/`](docs/evals/) written by the eval runner. + +| Metric | v1 — schema + image | v2 — + OCR text, normalisation rules | +| --- | ---: | ---: | +| Field accuracy (strict, every leaf) | 84.5% | **91.1%** | +| Value accuracy (leaves with a golden value) | 86.3% | **95.1%** | +| Documents fully correct | 36.8% | **50.0%** | +| `line_items` exact match | 42.1% | **66.7%** | +| `total` | 78.9% | 94.4% | +| `line_items[].name` | 73.9% | 81.6% | +| Not scored (truncated / rate-limited) | 1 / 0 | 0 / 2 | + +What v1 got wrong, from the per-document error listing: thousands separators read as decimals +(`"60.000"` → `60`), sub-items (toppings, add-ons) promoted to line items, and item names +"corrected" instead of copied. v2 spells those rules out and adds the OCR text next to the image. +The same analysis also caught a bug on the *golden* side — `"Rp. 111,000"` parsed as `111.0` — which +was fixed, the labels re-mapped, and v1 re-scored from its recordings. + +Prompt **v3** (three retrieved few-shot examples) and **v4** (evidence quotes, a self-check that the +line totals add up, one repair round) are implemented and registered; their measurements, the +ablations (no few-shot, image only, effort) and the 100-document runs are the next thing this README +gets. The free tier of the model above allows ~50 requests a day, which is what set the pace. + +![Comparison page: fields as rows, prompt versions as columns](docs/images/compare.png) + +## How it works + +```mermaid +flowchart LR + U[Upload / CORD import] --> R[Render pages
pypdfium2 · Pillow] + R --> O[OCR
RapidOCR: lines, words, boxes] + O --> E[Embed OCR text
fastembed · pgvector] + E --> F[Few-shot retrieval
labelled, never test split] + F --> M[Vision model, structured output
Claude · OpenRouter · Ollama] + M --> V[Validate · consistency check
one repair round] + V --> G[Ground values in OCR
confidence + boxes] + G --> S[(ExtractionRun
tokens · cost · latency)] + S --> UI[Review UI] & EV[Eval runner] +``` + +- **Schemas** ([`schemas/compiler.py`](backend/src/fieldwise/schemas/compiler.py)): an authored + JSON Schema is compiled into the strict schema structured outputs need (closed objects, every + property required, every leaf nullable) plus per-field metadata with a matcher (`money`, + `integer`, `text`, `list`). +- **Providers** ([`extraction/provider.py`](backend/src/fieldwise/extraction/provider.py), + [`openai_compat.py`](backend/src/fieldwise/extraction/openai_compat.py)): the Anthropic SDK + (cached system block, `output_config` with effort and a JSON-schema format, Batches API) and any + OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenRouter, a local Ollama, OpenAI) behind one protocol; a fake + provider for tests and a cassette provider that records and replays. +- **Grading** ([`evals/matchers.py`](backend/src/fieldwise/evals/matchers.py), ADR 0003): six + outcomes per leaf, lists aligned by position, money compared as decimals after the same + normalisation the importer applied, infrastructure failures in a sidecar and never in a denominator. +- **Review UI** (`web/`, Next.js 16): the page image with OCR boxes, the field tree with confidence, + the golden label side by side, corrections, run stats, eval comparison. + +## Quickstart + +```bash +git clone https://github.com/ilia-muravev-dev/fieldwise && cd fieldwise +cp backend/.env.example backend/.env # choose a provider below +just app # Postgres+pgvector, Redis, migrations, API :8000, worker, web :3000 +``` + +Pick a model provider in `backend/.env`: + +| Provider | Settings | Notes | +| --- | --- | --- | +| Anthropic | `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=…`, `DEFAULT_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5` | structured outputs, prompt caching, `--batch` at half price | +| OpenRouter | `LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-or-…`, `DEFAULT_MODEL=nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free` | free vision models exist; ~50 requests/day without credits | +| Ollama (local) | `LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1` (`http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1` from Docker), `OPENAI_API_KEY=ollama`, `DEFAULT_MODEL=qwen2.5vl:7b` | free and offline; slower | +| none | `LLM_PROVIDER=fake` | the stack runs, extractions return nulls (what the e2e tests use) | + +Then, from `backend/`: + +```bash +uv sync +uv run fieldwise ingest cord --split test --split validation # 200 labelled receipts (~480 MB download) +uv run fieldwise ocr run # RapidOCR, ~1 minute on a laptop +uv run fieldwise embed # bge-small embeddings for few-shot retrieval +uv run fieldwise extract cord-v2/test/0000 --prompt v2 # one document, with tokens, cost, latency +uv run fieldwise eval run --prompt v2 --limit 20 --cassette record # a measurement; asks before spending +uv run fieldwise eval compare --write # the table above +``` + +Open http://localhost:3000 for the review UI. Upload your own PDF or photo there; the worker runs OCR, +and "Run extraction" queues a model call you can watch land. + +## The eval loop, precisely + +1. `fieldwise eval run` prepares every request first, then executes them in a thread pool, one by + one, or as one Message Batch; a second phase runs the v4 repair turns. +2. Each extraction is graded against the document's golden label — a reviewer's correction wins + over the dataset label. Failed and truncated runs go to the sidecar with their cause. +3. Two headline numbers are always shown together: **strict** field accuracy (null agreements + count) and **value** accuracy (only leaves with a golden value), plus the document exact-match + rate, Wilson intervals per field, cost from the API's usage block, latency p50/p95. +4. Reports land in `docs/evals/` as Markdown and JSON; `eval compare` renders the README table. +5. CI (`eval-gate`) loads a committed bundle of 20 test receipts into a fresh database, replays the + recorded responses, re-scores them and fails on a > 2-point regression of any field. + +Few-shot examples come from labelled non-test documents only; the exclusion is in the SQL +(ADR 0004), and a test asserts a test document's identical twin is never retrieved. + +## Repository + +``` +backend/ Python 3.12 · FastAPI · SQLAlchemy 2 · Celery · Typer CLI · RapidOCR · fastembed · pgvector + src/fieldwise/{schemas,documents,extraction,retrieval,evals,api,worker,gate} + evals/cassettes/ recorded model responses evals/gate/ the CI fixture bundle +web/ Next.js 16 · React 19 · Tailwind 4 · shadcn · TanStack Query · typed client from openapi.json +docs/adr/ decisions docs/evals/ measurements openapi.json the API contract (checked in CI) +``` + +## Decisions + +| ADR | Decision | +| --- | --- | +| [0001](docs/adr/0001-evals-before-ui.md) | The eval harness comes before the UI; README numbers are copied from its reports | +| [0002](docs/adr/0002-rapidocr-over-tesseract.md) | RapidOCR (PP-OCR on ONNX, pip-only) over Tesseract | +| [0003](docs/adr/0003-how-extractions-are-graded.md) | Six outcomes per leaf; strict and value accuracy side by side; failures never scored | +| [0004](docs/adr/0004-few-shot-pool-excludes-the-test-split.md) | The few-shot pool structurally excludes the test split | +| [0005](docs/adr/0005-recorded-responses-make-ci-free.md) | Recorded responses make the CI gate free and deterministic | + +## Development + +```bash +just check # backend: ruff, mypy --strict, pytest (unit + pgvector testcontainer); openapi freshness; web: biome, tsc, vitest, build +just app-e2e # the stack with the fake provider +just e2e # Playwright: upload → OCR → extraction → correction +just openapi # regenerate openapi.json and the typed web client +``` + +Dataset: CORD (Park et al., 2019), CC BY 4.0; three downscaled receipts live in +`backend/tests/fixtures/cord` with attribution. License: [MIT](./LICENSE) © Ilia Muravev. diff --git a/docs/images/compare.png b/docs/images/compare.png new file mode 100644 Binary files /dev/null and b/docs/images/compare.png differ diff --git a/docs/images/review.png b/docs/images/review.png new file mode 100644 Binary files /dev/null and b/docs/images/review.png differ diff --git a/web/scripts/readme-shots.mjs b/web/scripts/readme-shots.mjs new file mode 100644 --- /dev/null +++ b/web/scripts/readme-shots.mjs @@ -0,0 +1,24 @@ +// Captures the README screenshots against a running stack: node scripts/readme-shots.mjs +import { chromium } from "@playwright/test"; + +const [docId, evalIds] = process.argv.slice(2); +const base = process.env.E2E_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000"; +const browser = await chromium.launch(); +const page = await browser.newPage({ + viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 }, + deviceScaleFactor: 1, +}); + +await page.goto(`${base}/documents/${docId}`); +await page.getByText("succeeded", { exact: true }).first().waitFor(); +await page.locator("li", { hasText: "total" }).last().getByRole("button").first().click(); +await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0)); +page.waitForTimeout(600); +await page.screenshot({ path: "../docs/images/review.png" }); + +await page.goto(`${base}/evals/compare?ids=${evalIds}`); +await page.getByText("Field accuracy (strict)").waitFor(); +await page.waitForTimeout(400); +await page.screenshot({ path: "../docs/images/compare.png" }); +await browser.close(); +console.log("wrote docs/images/review.png and compare.png");
